readings.title: Shameless Idolatry
readings.subtitle: Like a wild donkey in heat, Judah pursues foreign gods, claiming innocence despite overwhelming evidence.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 2:23] <dq>“How do <dn>you</dn> say, ‘<dn>I</dn> am not defiled, <dn>I</dn> have not gone after the Ba‛als’? See <dn>את</dn> <dn>your</dn> way in the valley, know what <dn>you</dn> have done: a swift dromedary breaking loose in her ways,</dq>
[24] <dq>a wild donkey used to the wilderness, sniffing the wind in the desire of her being – in her time of mating, who turns her away? All those who seek her need not weary themselves; in her month they find her.</dq>
[25] <dq>“Keep <dn>your</dn> foot from being bare, and <dn>your</dn> throat from thirst. But <dn>you</dn> said, ‘It is useless, because <dn>I</dn> love strangers, and after them <dn>I</dn> go.’</dq>
[26] <dq>“As the thief is ashamed when he is found out, so is the house of Yisra’ěl ashamed – they and their sovereigns and their heads, and their priests and their prophets,</dq>
[27] <dq>saying to a tree, ‘<dn>You</dn> are my father,’ and to a stone, ‘<dn>You</dn> gave birth to me.’ For they have turned their back to <dn>Me</dn>, and not their face. But in the time of their calamity they say, ‘Arise and save us.’</dq>
[28] <dq>“But where are <dn>your</dn> mighty ones that <dn>you</dn> have made for yourselves? Let them arise, see if they save <dn>you</dn> in the time of <dn>your</dn> calamity. Because <dn>your</dn> mighty ones have become as many as <dn>your</dn> cities, O Yehuḏah.</dq>
[29] <dq>“Why do <dn>you</dn> complain to <dn>Me</dn>? <dn>You</dn> all have transgressed against <dn>Me</dn>,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[30] <dq>“In vain have <dn>I</dn> stricken <dn>את</dn> <dn>your</dn> children – they received no instruction. <dn>Your</dn> sword has devoured <dn>your</dn> prophets like a destroying lion.</dq>
[31] <dq>“O generation, see <dn>את</dn> the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! Have <dn>I</dn> been a wilderness to Yisra’ěl, Or a land of darkness? Why do <dn>My</dn> people say, ‘We have broken loose; we come to <dn>You</dn> no more’?</dq>
[32] <dq>“Would a maiden forget her ornaments, or a bride her headband? Yet <dn>My</dn> people have forgotten <dn>Me</dn>, days without number.</dq>
[33] <dq>“Why do <dn>you</dn> embellish <dn>your</dn> way to seek love? Therefore <dn>you</dn> have even taught the evil women <dn>your</dn> ways.</dq>
[34] <dq>“Even on <dn>your</dn> skirts is found the blood of the lives of the poor innocents. <dn>You</dn> did not find them breaking in, but in spite of all these,</dq>
[35] <dq>you say, ‘Because <dn>I</dn> am innocent, certainly <dn>His</dn> displeasure shall turn from me.’ See, <dn>I</dn> shall bring judgment on <dn>you</dn>, because <dn>you</dn> say, ‘<dn>I</dn> have not sinned.’</dq>
[36] <dq>“Why do <dn>you</dn> go about so much to change <dn>your</dn> way? Even of Mitsrayim <dn>you</dn> are to be ashamed, as <dn>you</dn> were ashamed of Ashshur.</dq>
[37] <dq>“Even from this one <dn>you</dn> shall go forth, with <dn>your</dn> hands on <dn>your</dn> head. For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has rejected those <dn>you</dn> trust, and <dn>you</dn> shall not prosper by them.</dq>
[Jeremiah 3:1] <dn>Elohim</dn> said, <dq>“If a man puts away his wife, and she goes from him and becomes another man’s, does he return to her again? Would not that land be made greatly unclean? But <dn>you</dn> have committed whoring with many lovers. And would <dn>you</dn> return to <dn>Me</dn>?”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[2] <dq>“Lift up <dn>your</dn> eyes to the bare heights and see: where have <dn>you</dn> not lain with men? Besides the ways <dn>you</dn> have sat for them like an Araḇian in the wilderness. And <dn>you</dn> made the land unclean with <dn>your</dn> whorings and <dn>your</dn> evil.</dq>
[3] <dq>“Therefore the showers have been withheld, and there has been no latter rain. <dn>You</dn> have had a whore’s forehead, <dn>you</dn> refuse to be ashamed.</dq>
[4] <dq>“Shall <dn>you</dn> not from now on cry to <dn>Me</dn>, ‘<dn>My</dn> father, <dn>You</dn> are the guide of my youth?</dq>
[5] <dq>Does one bear a grudge forever? Does one keep it to the end?’ See, <dn>you</dn> have spoken and done the evils that <dn>you</dn> could.”</dq>

readings.title: Treacherous Judah and Backsliding Israel
readings.subtitle: In the days of King Josiah, YeHoVaH points out that Judah witnessed Israel's punishment for adultery but learned nothing, turning to Him with falsehood.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 3:6] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me in the days of Yoshiyahu the sovereign, <dq>“Have <dn>you</dn> seen <dn>את</dn> what backsliding Yisra’ěl has done? She has gone up on every high mountain and under every green tree, and there committed whoring.</dq>
[7] <dq>“And after she had done all these, <dn>I</dn> said ‘Return to <dn>Me</dn>.’ But she did not return. And her treacherous sister Yehuḏah saw it.</dq>
[8] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> saw that for all the causes for which backsliding Yisra’ěl had committed adultery, <dn>I</dn> had put her away and given her a certificate of divorce; yet her treacherous sister Yehuḏah did not fear, but went and committed whoring too.</dq>
[9] <dq>“And it came to be, through her frivolous whoring, that she defiled the land and committed adultery with stones and wood.</dq>
[10] <dq>“And yet for all this her treacherous sister Yehuḏah has not turned to <dn>Me</dn> with all her heart, but falsely,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: A Plea for Israel's Return
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH declares backsliding Israel more righteous than treacherous Judah and offers restoration if they will only acknowledge their guilt and return.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 3:11] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, <dq>“Backsliding Yisra’ěl has shown herself more righteous than treacherous Yehuḏah.</dq>
[12] <dq>“Go and proclaim these words toward the north, and say, ‘Return, O backsliding Yisra’ěl,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘<dn>I</dn> shall not look on <dn>you</dn> in displeasure, for <dn>I</dn> am lovingly-committed,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>’and <dn>I</dn> do not bear a grudge forever.</dq>
[13] <dq>Only, acknowledge <dn>את</dn> <dn>your</dn> crookedness, because <dn>you</dn> have transgressed against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>your</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>, and have scattered <dn>your</dn> ways to strangers under every green tree, and <dn>you</dn> have not obeyed <dn>My</dn> voice,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[14] <dq>“Return, O backsliding children,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“for <dn>I</dn> shall rule over <dn>you</dn>, and shall take <dn>you</dn>, one from a city and two from a clan, and shall bring <dn>you</dn> to Tsiyon.</dq>
[15] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall give <dn>you</dn> <dn>את</dn> shepherds according to <dn>My</dn> heart, and they shall feed <dn>you</dn> with knowledge and understanding.</dq>
[16] <dq>“And it shall be, when <dn>you</dn> have increased, and shall be fruitful in the land in those days,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“that they no longer say, ‘<dn>את</dn> The ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ Neither would it come to heart, nor would they remember it, nor would they visit it, nor would it be made again.</dq>
[17] <dq>“At that time Yerushalayim shall be called the throne of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and all the nations shall be gathered to it, to the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to Yerushalayim, and no longer walk after the stubbornness of their evil heart.</dq>
[18] <dq>“In those days the house of Yehuḏah shall go to the house of Yisra’ěl, and they shall come together out of the land of the north to the land that <dn>I</dn> have given as an inheritance to <dn>your</dn> fathers.</dq>
[19] <dq>“But <dn>I</dn> said, ‘How would <dn>I</dn> put <dn>you</dn> among <dn>את</dn> the children and give <dn>you</dn> <dn>את</dn> a pleasant land, a splendid inheritance of the hosts of nations?’ “And <dn>I</dn> said, ‘Call <dn>Me</dn>, “<dn>My</dn> Father,” and do not turn away from <dn>Me</dn>.’</dq>
[20] <dq>“But indeed as a wife betrays her husband, so have <dn>you</dn> betrayed <dn>Me</dn>, O house of Yisra’ěl,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[21] A voice was heard on the bare heights, weeping supplications of the children of Yisra’ěl, because they have perverted their way, they have forgotten <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn>.
[22] <dq>“Return, O backsliding children, <dn>I</dn> shall make <dn>your</dn> backslidings cease.”</dq> “See, we have come to <dn>You</dn>, for <dn>You</dn> are <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>.
[23] “Truly, delusion comes from the high hills, the noisy throng on the mountains. Truly, in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> is the deliverance of Yisra’ěl.
[24] “For shame has devoured the labour of our fathers from our youth, their flocks and their herds, their sons and their daughters.
[25] “We shall lie down in our shame, while our reproach covers us. For we have sinned against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, we and our fathers, from our youth even to this day, and have not obeyed the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>.”
[Jeremiah 4:1] <dq>“If <dn>you</dn> do return, O Yisra’ěl,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“return to <dn>Me</dn>. And if <dn>you</dn> remove <dn>your</dn> abominations from <dn>My</dn> presence, and cease straying,</dq>
[2] <dq>and shall swear, ‘As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives,’ in truth, in right-ruling, and in righteousness – then nations shall bless themselves in <dn>Him</dn>, and they shall boast in <dn>Him</dn>!”</dq>

readings.title: Break Up Your Fallow Ground
readings.subtitle: A call for heart-circumcision is followed by a dire warning of a destructive force coming from the north as judgment for rebellion.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 4:3] For this is what <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to the men of Yehuḏah and Yerushalayim, <dq>“Break up <dn>your</dn> tillable ground, and do not sow among thorns.</dq>
[4] <dq>"Circumcise yourselves unto <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and take away <dn>את</dn> the foreskins of <dn>your</dn> hearts, <dn>you</dn> men of Yehuḏah and inhabitants of Yerushalayim, lest <dn>My</dn> wrath come forth like fire and burn, with none to quench it, because of the evil of <dn>your</dn> deeds.”</dq>
[5] Declare in Yehuḏah and let it be heard in Yerushalayim, and say, <dq>“Blow a shophar in the land. Cry aloud and say, ‘Gather yourselves, and let us go into the walled city.’</dq>
[6] <dq>“Lift up <dn>את</dn> the banner toward Tsiyon. Be strong, do not stand still! For <dn>I</dn> am bringing evil from the north, and great destruction.”</dq>
[7] <dq>“A lion has come up from his bush, and the destroyer of nations is on his way. He has set out from his place to make <dn>your</dn> land a ruin. <dn>Your</dn> cities are laid waste, without inhabitant.</dq>
[8] <dq>“For this, gird yourself with sackcloth, lament and wail. For the burning displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has not turned back from us.</dq>
[9] <dq>“And in that day it shall be,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“that the heart of the sovereign shall perish, and the heart of the heads. And the priests shall be astonished, and the prophets wonder.”</dq>
[10] Then I said, “Ah, <dn>Master</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! Truly, <dn>You</dn> have greatly deceived this people and Yerushalayim, saying, ‘Peace is for <dn>you</dn>,’ whereas the sword reaches to the heart.”
[11] At that time it shall be said to this people and to Yerushalayim, <dq>“A scorching wind of the bare heights blows in the wilderness toward the daughter of <dn>My</dn> people, not to fan or to cleanse.</dq>
[12] <dq>“A wind too strong for this shall come for <dn>Me</dn>. Now it is <dn>I</dn> who speak judgments against them.</dq>
[13] “See, he comes up like clouds, and his chariots like a whirlwind. His horses shall be swifter than eagles. Woe to us, for we shall be ravaged!”
[14] O Yerushalayim, wash <dn>your</dn> heart from evil, and be saved. Till when would <dn>your</dn> wicked thoughts remain within <dn>you</dn>?
[15] For a voice is declaring from Dan, and is proclaiming trouble from Mount Ephrayim:
[16] “Announce to the nations, look, proclaim against Yerushalayim, that besiegers are coming from a distant land and raise their voice against the cities of Yehuḏah.
[17] “Like keepers of a field they are against her all around, because she has rebelled against <dn>את</dn> <dn>Me</dn>,” declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[18] <dq>“<dn>Your</dn> ways and <dn>your</dn> deeds have brought <dn>את</dn> this upon <dn>you</dn>. This is <dn>your</dn> evil, because it is bitter, because it has reached into <dn>your</dn> heart.”</dq>

readings.title: Jeremiah's Anguish
readings.subtitle: The prophet cries out in pain, his heart pounding at the sound of the shophar and the shout of battle for his foolish people.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 4:19] O my inward parts, my inward parts! I am in pain! O the walls of my heart! My heart pounds in me, I am not silent. For you have heard, O my being, a voice of a shophar, a shout of battle!
[20] Destruction upon destruction is cried, for all the land is ravaged. Suddenly my tents are ravaged – my curtains in a moment.
[21] How long shall I see a banner, and hear a voice of a shophar?
[22] <dq>“For <dn>My</dn> people are foolish, they have not known <dn>Me</dn>. They are stupid children, and they have no understanding. They are wise to do evil, but to do good they have no knowledge.”</dq>

readings.title: The Earth Returns to Chaos
readings.subtitle: Jeremiah sees a vision of the land made formless and empty, a reversal of creation, because of YeHoVaH's burning displeasure.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 4:23] I looked at the earth, and saw it was formless and empty. And the heavens, they had no light.
[24] I looked at the mountains, and saw they shook, and all the hills were swaying.
[25] I looked, and saw there was no man, and all the birds of the heavens had fled.
[26] I looked, and saw the garden land was a wilderness, and all its cities were broken down at the presence of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, by <dn>His</dn> burning displeasure.
[27] For thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“All the earth shall be a ruin, but <dn>I</dn> shall not make a complete end.</dq>
[28] <dq>“On account of this, let the earth mourn and the heavens above be dark, because <dn>I</dn> have spoken, because <dn>I</dn> have purposed and shall not relent, nor do <dn>I</dn> turn back from it.”</dq>
[29] All the city is fleeing from the noise of the horsemen and bowmen. They shall go into bushes and climb up on the rocks. All the city is forsaken, and no one is dwelling in it.
[30] And when you are ravaged, what would you do? Though you put on crimson, though you adorn yourself with ornaments of gold, though you enlarge your eyes with paint, you beautify yourself in vain. Your lovers despise you, they seek your life.
[31] For I have heard a voice as of a woman in labour, the distress as of her who brings forth her first child, the voice of the daughter of Tsiyon! She bewails herself, she spreads out her hands, saying, “Woe to me, for my being faints because of killers!”

readings.title: The Search for One Righteous Man
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH challenges Jeremiah to find even one person in Jerusalem who acts justly, but finds only deceit, rebellion, and betrayal from the poor to the great.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 5:1] <dq>“Diligently search the streets of Yerushalayim, and please look, and know and seek in her open places if <dn>you</dn> find <dn>את</dn> a man, if there is anyone doing right-ruling, seeking the truth, then <dn>I</dn> shall pardon her.</dq>
[2] “Even when they say, ‘As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives,’ they swear falsely, for certain.”
[3] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, are <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> eyes not on truth? <dn>You</dn> have stricken them, but they have not grieved. <dn>You</dn> have consumed them, but they have refused to receive instruction. They made their faces stronger than rock, they refused to turn back.
[4] Then I said, “These are only the poor. They have been foolish, for they have not known the way of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the right-ruling of their <dn>Elohim</dn>.
[5] “Let me go to the great men and speak to them, for they have known the way of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the right-ruling of their <dn>Elohim</dn>.” But these have altogether broken <dn>את</dn> the yoke and torn off <dn>את</dn> the bonds.
[6] Therefore a lion from the forest shall strike them, a wolf of the deserts ravage them. A leopard is watching over their cities, whoever comes out of them is torn in pieces. For their transgressions have been many, their backslidings have been numerous.
[7] <dq>“Why should <dn>I</dn> pardon <dn>you</dn> for this? <dn>Your</dn> children have forsaken <dn>Me</dn> and sworn by those that are not mighty ones. When <dn>I</dn> had filled them up, they then committed adultery and they thronged to the house of a whore.</dq>
[8] <dq>“They were like well-fed horses, every one neighed after his neighbour’s wife.</dq>
[9] <dq>“Would <dn>I</dn> not punish them for this?”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>“And would <dn>I</dn> not revenge <dn>Myself</dn> on such a nation as this?</dq>
[10] <dq>“Go up on her walls and destroy, but do not make a complete end. Take away <dn>את</dn> her branches, for they do not belong to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>
[11] <dq>“For the house of Yisra’ěl and the house of Yehuḏah have utterly betrayed <dn>Me</dn>,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[12] They have been untrue to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and said, “It is not <dn>He</dn>. No evil comes upon us, nor do we see sword or scarcity of food.”
[13] And the prophets have become wind, and the Word is not in them. Thus shall be done to them:
[14] Therefore thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of hosts, <dq>“Because <dn>you</dn> speak this word, see, <dn>I</dn> am making <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> words in <dn>your</dn> mouth fire, and <dn>את</dn> this people wood, and it shall devour them.</dq>
[15] <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am bringing <dn>את</dn> a nation against <dn>you</dn> from afar, O house of Yisra’ěl,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>“It is an enduring nation, it is an ancient nation, a nation whose language <dn>you</dn> do not know, nor do <dn>you</dn> understand what they say.</dq>
[16] <dq>“Their quiver is like an open burial-site, all of them are mighty men.</dq>
[17] <dq>“And they shall eat up <dn>את</dn> <dn>your</dn> harvest and <dn>את</dn> <dn>your</dn> bread, which <dn>your</dn> sons and daughters should eat. They shall eat up <dn>את</dn> <dn>your</dn> flocks and <dn>את</dn> <dn>your</dn> herds, they shall eat up <dn>את</dn> <dn>your</dn> vines and <dn>את</dn> <dn>your</dn> fig trees. With the sword they shall demolish <dn>את</dn> <dn>your</dn> walled cities, in which <dn>you</dn> are trusting.</dq>
[18] <dq>“But even in those days,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> shall not make a complete end of <dn>you</dn>.</dq>
[19] <dq>“And it shall be, when they say, ‘Why does <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> do all this to us?’ then <dn>you</dn> shall answer them, ‘As <dn>you</dn> have forsaken <dn>Me</dn> and served foreign mighty ones in <dn>your</dn> land, so <dn>you</dn> shall serve foreigners in a land that is not <dn>yours</dn>.’</dq>
